concept: FDE Interview Practice And Timed Mock
title: FDE Interview Practice And Timed Mock Checkpoint

questions.prompt: An interviewer asks you to automate support. What should precede a detailed architecture?

options.label: Assume all support actions may run autonomously.
Clarify the user, task, constraints, data and success criteria.
Name as many infrastructure services as possible.

questions.explanation: Clarification creates a problem contract. Tool lists and unsupported authority assumptions skip the core ambiguity the exercise probes.

questions.prompt: In the architecture mock, what does the outbox alone fail to guarantee?

options.label: That a remote effect cannot repeat after remote success and a worker crash.
That local dispatch intent can be stored with the job.
That a transaction can contain multiple local records.

questions.explanation: An outbox preserves local dispatch intent. Remote-effect idempotency or reconciliation addresses a separate failure window.

options.label: A teammate's achievement retold as entirely your own.
A fabricated customer story with an impressive metric.
A factual account of your decision, alternatives, evidence, limitation and learning.

questions.explanation: Specific, honest ownership can withstand follow-up questions. Misattribution and invented outcomes undermine the evidence the interviewer needs.

questions.prompt: What does a score of 18/24 in this mock mean?

options.label: It meets an authored practice heuristic, not an employer hiring threshold.
It guarantees passing an FDE interview.

questions.explanation: The rubric structures rehearsal only. Employers and production contexts evaluate additional evidence under different constraints.
